objective: I can name at least three next-step options: college/sixth form, apprenticeship/training and employment with training/support.

calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 2, 11–15 January 2027. Tuesday 12 January 2027, P3. One 40-minute formative lesson for up to five learners. Spring 1 runs 4 January–12 February, six weeks; Week 6 assessing. Source Week 5 retains its mixed evidence role. No clock time supplied.
source_adaptation: Exact E17 weekly outcome, F17 focus, G17 lesson outcome and J17 evidence retained. H17 sequence and I17 timing retained. Generic invented cards replace local examples under the owner rule. Route icons, learn/earn/both sorting, accessible explanation of FE, sixth form, independent training provision and apprenticeships, plus private optional choice check are included. Review is private. K17 reduced choices, visual model and usual access are retained; websites replaced by prepared in-pack cards. Aspire is an optional extension. A paid apprenticeship is distinguished from a training course without a paid job. Earn in F describes only the information supplied; missing learning/support is investigated rather than treated as a complete route.

sources.note: Physical row 17 is Spring 1 row 2. E17 weekly outcome, F17 focus, G17 lesson outcome and J17 evidence verified exactly. H17 sequence and I17 timing retained. Local examples become invented unnamed cards under owner instruction; website suggestions replaced by in-pack material. Named source-only qualification terms omitted. Raw workbook not distributed.
Accepted BUILD Week 1 supplies clean layout, folder shape, generic picture bank and retrieval continuity. This lesson uses row 17 outcomes, sequence and evidence.

Tuesday 12 January 2027 P3. Exact lesson outcome; route types only, with no named college, provider, employer or place. Same BUILD rules as accepted Week 1, up to five learners, 40 minutes. Next Weeks 3–6 one per return. GROW Careers remains paused. Pause for Downloaded.

source_end_check: Can the student name three different next-step routes?
source_sequence_verbatim: Arrival/retrieval linked to previous careers learning → I Do: explain/model what can i do after school? with concrete examples → We Do: guided sorting/annotating/scenario discussion → You Do: Use route icons and local examples; sort 'learn / earn / both'; explain FE, sixth form, ITP and apprenticeship in accessible language; personal choice check. → 1:1/whole-class review → exit check and add evidence to Careers Portfolio.
timing: Recall that careers can change and learning or help can support a next step.
Pre-teach route words; explain three options with icons and model A.
Sort C and D; discuss F, then check the difference between pay and learning.
Name all three option groups in a post-16 options grid; sort B and E; optional private choice check.
Check three different groups, one NS and reply; bank the options grid in Careers Portfolio.

routes.Supported: Keep all three option cards and the word bank. Read one short section at a time. Offer two labels per choice, then return the full set. Point, sign, type or use an exact scribe. Record labels supplied or answers modelled.
routes.Independent: Name all three option groups in the grid with normal reading and communication aids. Match B and E and give a clue from each. Use the cards to check.
routes.Aspire: Explain why C and D share option 2 but have different pay information. Give a useful question about F. Extra writing and public sharing are not required.

choices.label: Whole grid
choices.task: Use all three option cards to make the three-row options grid.

choices.label: One row at a time
choices.task: Choose between two option labels with an adult, then build each row of the same grid. Return the full set and check three different groups.

options.label: College/sixth form
options.meaning: Study courses and learn. A college may offer many subjects or job skills. A sixth form offers courses after school.

options.label: Apprenticeship/training
options.meaning: An apprenticeship is a paid job with planned learning. A training course teaches skills. A course may not include a paid job.

options.label: Employment with training/support
options.meaning: Do a paid job with training or help to do the work. Ask what learning and support are in place.

cases.text: A person takes a course at a college. They learn skills. This card has no paid job.
A person studies courses in a sixth form. This card has no paid job.
A person is an apprentice. They have a paid job and planned learning.
A person takes a training course to learn job skills. This card has no paid job.
A person has a paid job packing boxes. Staff train them and help them at work.
A card says a person has a paid job. It says nothing about learning or support.

colour_blind_safe: Icons, captions, group numbers and words carry meaning; no colour-only codes.
worked_examples_status: All worked examples, people and route situations are invented and generic. Pictures are symbols of learning or work, not real places or portraits. No real college, provider, employer, person, place, product or platform is named.
private_help_route: Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write a request or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. No personal finances, family jobs or public future-plan statements requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Either task can use Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank option and example fields. Save through the usual routine with lesson code and work reference; show an adult privately. Scribe exact words or selections, read back and allow correction. Separate usual access from supplied answers.
worked_example_and_fade: After model A, ask privately: A learn or B both? Key A; the card shows study and no paid job. If unsure, point to the exact clue and model again. Keep the word bank, names and icons; fade only answer cues. Do not remove normal communication access.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: three labelled icons, short examples, model and two-choice route. Communication and Interaction: pre-teach words, one instruction, processing time, frames and usual aid. SEMH: calm stages, pass, supported pause/return, no public questioning. Sensory and Physical: clear text and pictures, no colour-only codes, pointing instead of moving cards. EAL: plan in any language; explain route words before using abbreviations.
misconceptions: A paid apprenticeship includes planned learning; not all training courses include pay. A paid job card with no learning/support information is incomplete, not proof that support is absent. College, sixth form and training routes vary; they are not ranked by ability or worth. Real routes can overlap. Do not treat a tentative choice as fixed.

main_hinge.claim: Not every training course includes a paid job; check details.

parallel_hinge.claim: C shows both a paid job and planned learning.

success: Name or identify all three broad option groups.
Match B and E to their route groups and sort the information shown as learn, earn or both.
Notice missing learning/support information and identify a useful question.

evidence.description: Post-16 options grid. Keep actual three group names/selections, B/E matches and sorting, access, answer prompts, first response, one NS and reply.

assessment: Exact source evidence: Post-16 options grid. Keep three option names/selections, B and E matches, learn/earn/both decisions, first response, access, answer prompts, one NS and reply. Secure core evidence identifies all three groups; do not count college and sixth form as two separate groups while omitting another. Accept accessible equivalent words that retain the route distinction, including learning/support with employment. Record naming separately from example sorting. A pass is unobserved; retain partial evidence. An optional preference is never marked right or wrong.
where_this_leads: This helps me name options after school and ask what I need to find out next.

Name three broad groups of next-step options. College and sixth form sit in the first group. Apprenticeship and training sit in the second; not every training course is a paid job. The third is employment with training/support. Groups may overlap in real life. This is an introduction, not an entry or eligibility decision.

Identify all three groups using words, cards or a usual communication aid. Link examples to the type of route and sort the information shown as learn, earn or both. Notice when learning or support information is missing.

5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes, following I17. Processing time and brief pauses are included. Slides 7 and 8 share the 23–35-minute task window.

0–5: choose learning a skill or asking for help as a useful response when a work plan changes. Supply the Week 1 idea if absent. 5–9: read the exact outcome and pre-teach option, learn, earn and both. 9–13: show all three route icons and explain the names. FE means further education after school; a college can offer it. A sixth form offers courses after school. An independent training provider is a type of organisation that teaches job skills; it is not a separate fourth group. Model A: option 1, learn, because the card describes study and no paid job.

13–19: compare C apprenticeship, both, with D training course, learn. Both belong to option 2; a paid apprenticeship is different from a course without a paid job. Discuss F: earn is all the card tells us; the next question is what learning or support comes with it. Do not present F as a complete recommended route. 19–23: private hinge, feedback and parallel check if needed.

23–35: whole grid or one row at a time. Both name all three groups and match B and E. For reduced choices offer 1/2 for B, 2/3 for E, then ask for the unused group 2 from 1/2. Return all three cards to check different groups. Log all choices and supplied labels. Optional personal choice check: which option would you like to find out more about? Not sure, pass or choosing for a made-up person are equally valid. No reason or personal history is required.

35–38: privately check three different groups, give one NS and retain the reply. 38–40: name or point to all three groups, or correct a missing/duplicate group. Keep the actual post-16 options grid in Careers Portfolio. A preference is not a commitment or part of the attainment judgement.

Keep all three option cards and the word bank. Read one short section at a time. Offer two labels per choice, then return the full set. Point, sign, type or use an exact scribe. Record labels supplied or answers modelled.
Name all three option groups in the grid with normal reading and communication aids. Match B and E and give a clue from each. Use the cards to check.
Explain why C and D share option 2 but have different pay information. Give a useful question about F. Extra writing and public sharing are not required.

After model A, ask privately: A learn or B both? Key A; the card shows study and no paid job. If unsure, point to the exact clue and model again. Keep the word bank, names and icons; fade only answer cues. Do not remove normal communication access.

Main: does every training course include a paid job? A yes; B no, check the course details. Key B. If unclear, compare C with D and repeat the distinction. Parallel: C has a paid job and planned learning. A both; B earn only. Key A. Pass is unobserved. Record the actual response and recheck privately.

Cognition and Learning: three labelled icons, short examples, model and two-choice route. Communication and Interaction: pre-teach words, one instruction, processing time, frames and usual aid. SEMH: calm stages, pass, supported pause/return, no public questioning. Sensory and Physical: clear text and pictures, no colour-only codes, pointing instead of moving cards. EAL: plan in any language; explain route words before using abbreviations.

Prompt ladder: 1 point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 give scaffold/choice; 5 model the first step only, then return the task. In I Do point to learning and work clues; in We Do prompt the wording; in You Do record actual help without silently completing the grid.

Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write a request or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. No personal finances, family jobs or public future-plan statements requested.

Either task can use Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank option and example fields. Save through the usual routine with lesson code and work reference; show an adult privately. Scribe exact words or selections, read back and allow correction. Separate usual access from supplied answers.

Exact source evidence: Post-16 options grid. Keep three option names/selections, B and E matches, learn/earn/both decisions, first response, access, answer prompts, one NS and reply. Secure core evidence identifies all three groups; do not count college and sixth form as two separate groups while omitting another. Accept accessible equivalent words that retain the route distinction, including learning/support with employment. Record naming separately from example sorting. A pass is unobserved; retain partial evidence. An optional preference is never marked right or wrong.

A paid apprenticeship includes planned learning; not all training courses include pay. A paid job card with no learning/support information is incomplete, not proof that support is absent. College, sixth form and training routes vary; they are not ranked by ability or worth. Real routes can overlap. Do not treat a tentative choice as fixed.

Give one NS, such as add the third group or explain why C is both. VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual banked evidence. R follows Voice, Audience, NS and a reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping.

All example people and route descriptions are invented, simplified and generic. Icons show learning or work, not real places or portraits. No named college, provider, employer, place, product or platform. No claims about actual availability, fees, pay amounts, eligibility or entry grades. Staff check age, entry and ongoing learning requirements through the usual advice route before a real decision. Listen calmly to concerns, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow normal procedures.

I can name at least three next-step options: college/sixth form, apprenticeship/training and employment with training/support.

1 College/sixth form; 2 apprenticeship/training; 3 employment with training/support. The assessment asks for coverage of all three broad groups, not three labels from the same group. Accept accessible equivalent words that preserve the distinction. Learners may select a label with their usual aid; record how it was identified.

A college may offer further education, including subjects or job skills. A sixth form offers courses after school, within a school or college. An apprenticeship combines a paid job with planned learning. A training course teaches skills but may not include a paid job. An independent training provider is a generic type of organisation teaching job skills; it can deliver training and is not an additional fourth route group. Employment with training/support means a job with learning or help in place. Actual routes overlap and vary; this introductory grid is not a complete taxonomy or an eligibility judgement.

Retrieve Week 1: work plans can change, and learning a skill or asking for help may support a next step. Model A: group 1, learn. Explain the course and no-paid-job clues. Model check A learn versus B both: key A.

C: group 2, both, because a paid apprenticeship includes planned learning. D: group 2, learn, because this training course has no paid job. Main hinge B: not every training course has a paid job; check details. Parallel A: C is both. Re-model C/D privately if unclear, then recheck. A pass is unobserved.

The completed grid identifies all three groups. Example B matches group 1, learn; it describes sixth form study and no paid job. E matches group 3, both; it describes a paid job, training and help. Group 2 must still be named even though B and E match the other groups. Either C or D can be offered as its example.

F gives pay only, so the information sort is earn. It gives no basis for deciding what learning/support is available. Ask what training or help comes with the job. Do not infer none, count F as a full supported-employment route, or present earn alone as a complete recommendation. The sort concerns the text of the card, not a judgement about every real route.

Whole grid: all three option cards with B and E. One row at a time: B with labels 1/2; E with 2/3; then remaining group 2 with 1/2. Return the full set and check all three distinct groups. Record offered labels, fixed choices and supplied answers separately from usual communication access.

Offer one option to find out more about, not sure, pass or choice for an invented person. Do not ask for a public reason or family plans. Mark neither the preference nor the decision to pass. It is a tentative enquiry, not a destination decision.

Check naming and sorting separately. Useful NS: add the missing group; include training/support with the job; or show the paid-job and learning clues. Retain the first response and reply. Exit checks all three labels using speech, pointing or the usual aid. No hierarchy of route worth.

Exact evidence: Post-16 options grid. Secure core naming covers all three groups. Record B/E matches and sorts separately; retain partial evidence. Record actual cues, modelled answers, first attempt, one NS and reply. A no-response or pass is unobserved. Do not mark an optional preference or infer readiness for a real application.

Evidence Sheet page 2 has blank option fields, B/E fields, clue, optional choice and NS/reply. Either task route can be typed. Save with the usual routine, lesson code and work reference; share privately. Exact scribe reads back and allows correction. No online system needed.

E is actual banked work. R follows Voice, Audience, one NS and the learner’s reply. Add the grid to Careers Portfolio; offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping from actual work.

Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. Pass, supported pause/return and usual aids remain available. No real family finances, job histories or public plans requested. Listen calmly to concerns, avoid probing and secrecy promises and follow normal procedures. Keep concerns outside shared work.
